name: Japan
description: Japan offers expats an unparalleled blend of safety, efficiency, and a rich cultural experience. It attracts individuals seeking high-quality public services, unique lifestyle, and diverse economic opportunities, particularly in major urban centers.
longdescription: Expat life in Japan is characterized by a high standard of living, exceptional safety, and a meticulously organized society. While cities like Tokyo offer vibrant modern amenities and diverse career paths, especially in IT, healthcare, and specialized industries, living costs can be significantly higher than in other regions. The culture, deeply rooted in respect, punctuality, and community, can present a significant culture shock for newcomers, particularly regarding social cues, communication styles, and the continued reliance on traditional paperwork despite technological advancements. Healthcare is universal and high-quality, with all residents, including expats staying over three months, required to enroll in public insurance schemes, covering about 70% of costs. The economy is robust, though expats may find average local salaries lower than in some Western countries, which can be balanced by a generally lower cost of living outside of central Tokyo. Integrating into society often requires effort to overcome language barriers and build local support networks, but the rewards include access to a unique cultural heritage and a highly efficient daily life.

visas.name: Digital Nomad Visa (Designated Activities)
visas.description: This visa, officially designated as 'Specified Visa: Designated Activities (Digital Nomad, Spouse or Child of Digital Nomad)', allows remote workers and their accompanying spouse and children to reside in Japan for up to six months. It specifically permits working remotely for companies or clients based outside of Japan, offering an opportunity to experience Japanese life without engaging in local employment.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are remote workers or freelancers from eligible countries who earn income from foreign sources and wish to live in Japan temporarily.
visas.path_to_residency_description: This visa does not offer a direct path to permanent residency or any other long-term residency status in Japan.
visas.renewal_conditions: Not renewable; applicants must leave Japan and spend a continuous six-month period outside the country before reapplying for a new Digital Nomad Visa.
visas.tax_implications: Holders of this visa are generally considered non-residents for tax purposes if their stay in any calendar year is under 183 days. Foreign-sourced income is typically not subject to Japanese income tax. Japan has double taxation treaties with many countries to prevent dual taxation.
benefits: Ability to live and work remotely from Japan for up to six months.
Spouse and children are eligible to accompany the primary visa holder.
Freedom to travel domestically within Japan.
Not subject to Japanese income tax on foreign-sourced income if staying under 183 days.
required_documents: Visa application form (with a photo)
Valid passport
Documents explaining planned activities and period of stay in Japan
Documents proving annual income of JPY 10 million or more (e.g., tax payment certificate, income certificate, employment/business contracts)
Documents proving private health insurance coverage for death, injury, or illness during stay in Japan (compensation for medical treatment for injury or illness must be JPY 10 million or more)
Marriage certificate (if spouse is accompanying)
Birth certificate or equivalent (if child is accompanying)
Certificate of Eligibility (optional, but speeds up processing)
application_process_steps: Confirm eligibility criteria (nationality, income, insurance).
Gather all required documents, including proof of income and health insurance.
Obtain a Certificate of Eligibility (COE) from the Immigration Services Agency in Japan (optional, but recommended to expedite the process).
Complete the visa application form and submit it, along with a valid passport and passport-sized photo, to a Japanese embassy or consulate in your home country.
Pay the application fee.
Await visa approval (typically 2-8 weeks, but can vary).

visas.name: Highly Skilled Professional (i)(a) (Advanced Academic Research Activities)
visas.description: The Highly Skilled Professional (i)(a) visa is designed to attract foreign researchers, scientists, and educators to Japan. It enables individuals with high-level expertise to engage in advanced academic research, research guidance, or education activities under a contract with a Japanese public or private organization, contributing to Japan's economic growth and innovation.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are foreign nationals qualified to work in research, research guidance, or education at a Japanese university or research institution under a salary-based contract.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Holders of the Highly Skilled Professional visa can apply for permanent residency (PR) in an expedited manner. If the applicant maintains a score of 70-79 points, they are eligible to apply for PR after 3 years of continuous residence in Japan. If they maintain a score of 80 points or more, they can apply for PR after only 1 year of continuous residence. PR application requires demonstrating good conduct, stable income, consistent tax and pension payments, and securing a guarantor.
visas.renewal_conditions: To continue stay beyond the initial 5-year period, applicants must apply for a renewal or transition to the Highly Skilled Professional (ii) status or Permanent Residency before the current visa expires. The HSP (ii) visa grants an indefinite period of stay, allowing engagement in almost all work qualification activities.
benefits: Permission to engage in multiple types of activities (e.g., research and related business activities).
Initial period of stay granted for 5 years.
Fast-track to permanent residency (1 year for 80+ points, 3 years for 70+ points).
Permission for spouse to work in Japan.
Permission for parent(s) or a domestic worker to accompany under specific conditions.
Preferential and expedited processing of entry and residence procedures.
required_documents: Highly Skilled Professional Point Calculation Table with supporting evidence for all claimed points.
Application form for Certificate of Eligibility (CoE) or change of status.
ID photo (4 x 3cm, taken within six months prior to application).
Copy of applicant's passport.
Resume.
Proof of academic/professional qualifications (e.g., diplomas).
Employment contract with a Japanese public or private organization.
Documents from the employer (company information).
Proof of expected annual salary/income documents.
Bank deposit certificate (may be required for CoE application).
For dependants: marriage certificate, birth certificate, family register, and official documents showing the highly-skilled professional's annual household income.
All non-Japanese documents typically require certified Japanese translations.
application_process_steps: Self-assess points using the official points calculation table, ensuring a minimum of 70 points.
Have a sponsoring employer in Japan apply for a Certificate of Eligibility (CoE) at a regional immigration bureau on the applicant's behalf.
Once the CoE is issued, submit it along with other required documents to a Japanese embassy or consulate in the applicant's home country to apply for the Highly Skilled Professional visa.
Enter Japan, where the status of residence 'Highly Skilled Professional (i)(a)' will be granted.
For those already in Japan, apply for a change of status of residence at the local Immigration Services Agency office.

visas.name: Highly Skilled Professional (i)(b) (Advanced Specialized/Technical Activities)
visas.description: The Highly Skilled Professional (i)(b) visa is designed for foreign nationals possessing exceptional expertise and skills in advanced specialized or technical activities. It aims to attract individuals who can contribute to Japan's economic growth and innovation by engaging in work requiring knowledge or skills in natural sciences or humanities based on a contract with a public or private organization in Japan.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are highly skilled professionals, such as engineers and IT professionals, with strong academic backgrounds, extensive professional experience, and competitive incomes, who can meet a minimum points threshold of 70 points.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Holders of the Highly Skilled Professional (i) visa can apply for Permanent Residency (PR) after 3 years if they maintain 70 points or more, or after 1 year if they maintain 80 points or more. After maintaining HSP (i) status for 3 years, it's also possible to switch to Highly Skilled Professional (ii) status, which grants an indefinite period of stay.
visas.renewal_conditions: Must continue to score at least 70 points in the points evaluation system at the time of renewal.
benefits: Permission to engage in multiple related professional activities, including running a side business related to the primary field.
Initial visa validity of 5 years, providing significant stability and fewer renewals.
Accelerated path to Permanent Residency: 3 years of continuous residence for those with 70+ points, or 1 year for those with 80+ points.
Spouse may work in Japan in a wider range of occupations without meeting specific educational or work experience requirements.
Under certain income conditions, the ability to bring parents to Japan to assist with childcare for children under 7, or if the spouse is pregnant.
Priority processing for visa and residence applications.
required_documents: Application form for a Certificate of Eligibility (or application for permission to change status of residence).
Photograph (4cm x 3cm).
Applicant's passport and residence card (to be presented).

Points calculation table, along with supporting documents to prove each claimed point (e.g., academic background certificates, work experience certificates, annual income documentation, qualifications, Japanese language proficiency proof).
Certificate of Eligibility (COE) - original or a copy.
Visa application form (one or two depending on nationality).
Copy of Chinese Family Register and Temporary Residence Permit/Residence Certificate (for Chinese nationals).
application_process_steps: Check eligibility by calculating points based on academic background, professional experience, annual income, age, and other criteria (must score 70+ points).
Secure an employment contract with a public or private organization in Japan.
Prepare all necessary supporting documents, including those for the points calculation.
The prospective employer in Japan typically applies for a Certificate of Eligibility (COE) on behalf of the applicant to the Immigration Services Agency of Japan.
Once the COE is issued, submit the visa application along with the COE and other required documents to a Japanese Embassy or Consulate-General in the applicant's country of residence.
Undergo immigration procedures upon arrival in Japan.

visas.name: Highly Skilled Professional (i)(c) (Advanced Business Management Activities)
visas.description: The Highly Skilled Professional (i)(c) visa targets foreign nationals engaged in advanced business management activities in Japan, such as operating international trade or managing businesses at public or private organizations. It aims to attract highly skilled talent who can contribute to Japan's economic growth and introduce innovation to Japanese industry.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are company executives, directors, or senior managers with advanced business management experience and skills, involved in Japanese business operations.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Eligible to apply for permanent residency after maintaining Highly Skilled Professional (i) status for three consecutive years with 70 or more points. For those maintaining 80 or more points, the period is shortened to just one year.
visas.renewal_conditions: Must continue to maintain a score of 70 points or higher in the points evaluation system.
benefits: Permission to engage in multiple professional activities, offering broader work scope.
Initial five-year period of stay.
Accelerated path to permanent residency, with eligibility after 1 or 3 years.
Spouse may work in Japan with expanded work opportunities.
Parents may accompany under specific conditions for childcare (e.g., child under 7, or spouse is pregnant, and certain income conditions are met).
Permission to hire a foreign domestic worker under specific conditions (e.g., child under 13).
Preferential and expedited processing for immigration and residence procedures.
required_documents: Passport
Visa application form
Photograph (4x3cm, taken within six months)
Certificate of Eligibility (COE) - original or copy
Applicant's points calculation form
Applicant's resume
Applicant's bank deposit certificate (often required for dependants or financial stability proof)
Certificate of academic and qualifications (if any)
Other supplementary proof for obtaining points (e.g., employment verification letters for professional experience)
Official documents showing the highly-skilled foreign professional's annual household income (for dependants)
Other supplementary documents requested by the Immigration Bureau
application_process_steps: Employer/sponsor applies for a Certificate of Eligibility (COE) with a Highly Skilled Professional (i)(c) notation (including points calculation and activity type) from the Immigration Services Agency of Japan.
The Certificate of Eligibility (COE) is issued by the Immigration Services Agency.
The applicant applies for the visa at a Japanese embassy or consulate in their home country, submitting the COE and other required documents.
Upon approval, the applicant enters Japan and is granted the Highly Skilled Professional (i)(c) status of residence.

visas.name: Highly Skilled Professional (ii)
visas.description: The Highly Skilled Professional (ii) visa in Japan is a status of residence for foreign nationals who have engaged in activities as a Highly Skilled Professional (i) for at least three years and continue to meet specific criteria. It grants an indefinite period of stay in Japan, eliminating the need for future visa renewals and offering a broad scope of permitted activities.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are foreign professionals who have successfully maintained the Highly Skilled Professional (i) status for at least three years in Japan and continue to possess advanced, specialized skills and qualifications.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The Highly Skilled Professional (ii) status grants an indefinite period of stay, which is similar to permanent residency. Additionally, individuals who obtain HSP (i) can apply for permanent residency after 3 years (if maintaining 70-79 points) or 1 year (if maintaining 80+ points), providing a significantly accelerated path compared to standard visas.
visas.renewal_conditions: While providing an indefinite period of stay, the status can be jeopardized by prolonged unemployment. Holders must maintain good conduct, consistent and timely payment of all taxes and social insurance (pension and health insurance premiums), and continue to meet the requirements of a highly skilled professional.
benefits: Indefinite period of stay, removing the need for visa renewals.
Permission to engage in a wider range of professional activities, often encompassing almost all work qualification categories.
Spouse is permitted to work in a broader range of occupations than standard dependent visas.
Ability to bring parents to Japan under specific conditions (e.g., for childcare, with an annual household income over JPY 8 million).
Ability to bring a foreign domestic worker to Japan under specific conditions (e.g., with an annual household income over JPY 10 million).
Relaxation of residency history requirements for obtaining permanent residency (accelerated path from HSP (i) applies).
Flexibility to change employers without needing to apply for a change in status of residence, unlike HSP (i).
required_documents: Application for Permission to Change Status of Residence
Passport
Residence Card
Documents proving continuous residence for over 3 years under Highly Skilled Professional (i) status
Highly Skilled Professional Point Calculation Table (current score of 70 points or more)
Documents supporting claimed points (e.g., diplomas, certificates of academic/professional qualifications, employment contracts, proof of annual salary)
Certificates of employment and income (including tax certificates for national and local taxes for the required years)
Proof of public pension and health insurance premium payments for the required period (typically the last 2-3 years)
ID photo (4 x 3 cm, taken within six months prior to application)
application_process_steps: Maintain Highly Skilled Professional (i) status for at least three years (note: it's possible to change to HSP (ii) one year after entering Japan under certain J-Skip conditions, but generally 3 years are required).
Ensure you meet or exceed 70 points on the official Highly Skilled Professional points evaluation system at the time of application.
Gather all required documents, including proof of academic and professional qualifications, employment history, income, tax payments, and social insurance contributions.
Submit an 'Application for Permission to Change Status of Residence' along with the required documents to the regional Immigration Services Agency office.
Pay the application fee (revenue stamp).
Await the review and decision from the Immigration Services Agency.

visas.name: Special Highly Skilled Professional (J-Skip)
visas.description: The Special Highly Skilled Professional (J-Skip) visa is a Japanese work visa introduced in April 2023, designed to attract top-tier foreign professionals. It offers a streamlined path to residency and expanded preferential treatment beyond the traditional Highly Skilled Professional (HSP) visa system, primarily based on academic or professional background and a high annual income.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are highly skilled professionals such as researchers, engineers, or senior managers with advanced expertise and substantial annual income, seeking to work and reside long-term in Japan.
visas.path_to_residency_description: J-Skip holders can apply for permanent residency in Japan after just one year of continuous residence.
visas.renewal_conditions: Must maintain the specified income thresholds and comply with Japanese laws, including proper payment of national health insurance premiums and taxes.
benefits: Fast-track to Permanent Residency: eligibility to apply after just 1 year of residence.
Relaxed work requirements for spouses, allowing full-time employment in specialized roles.
Easier sponsorship of up to two foreign domestic staff under certain conditions (e.g., household income over 30 million JPY).
Priority lane access at major Japanese airports for faster immigration processing.
Permitting multiple residence activities.
required_documents: Application form for Certificate of Eligibility (COE) - varies by activity type (Professor, Research, Business Manager, Engineer, etc.).
One photograph (4cm × 3cm, white background, taken within 3 months).
Return Envelope (self-addressed with postage stamps for registered mail in Japan, if applying for COE within Japan).
Activity-related Documents (e.g., employment contract, company registration for business, research plan).
Proof of Education (diploma, degree certificate).
Proof of Work Experience (certificate of employment stating duties and period).
Documents showing expected annual income in Japan (e.g., employment contract, offer letter, income certificate, tax certificate).
Valid Passport.
Medical certificate.
Police clearance certificate.
application_process_steps: Your host institution (employer or university) in Japan applies for a Certificate of Eligibility (COE) at the Immigration Services Agency.
Gather and arrange all required documents, including the COE.
Fill out the visa application form.
Apply for the visa at the Japanese Embassy or Consulate-General in your country of residence (using the issued COE).
Attend an interview with a Japanese Immigration Officer if requested.
Wait for the final decision on the visa application.

visas.name: Specified Skilled Worker Type 1
visas.description: The Specified Skilled Worker Type 1 program is a work visa designed for foreign nationals possessing a certain degree of expertise and skills in specific industrial fields experiencing labor shortages in Japan. It allows them to work immediately in these sectors without requiring a university degree.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are foreign workers who can demonstrate job-ready skills and Japanese language ability in one of the designated industries facing labor shortages, typically without requiring a university degree.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Specified Skilled Worker Type 1 itself does not lead directly to permanent residency as the total stay is capped at 5 years and dependants are not allowed. However, it is often considered a pathway to Specified Skilled Worker Type 2 status, which has no upper limit on the length of stay, allows family accompaniment, and is considered a pathway toward long-term residency in Japan.
visas.renewal_conditions: Periods of stay are issued in 1-year, 6-month, or 4-month blocks, with a total cumulative maximum stay of 5 years. Renewal is subject to maintaining employment in the specified field and complying with visa conditions.
visas.tax_implications: Salaries for Specified Skilled Workers must be equal to or higher than what Japanese workers in the same role receive, implying standard Japanese income tax rules apply. No special tax exemptions or treatments are mentioned.
benefits: Easy to find work in industries facing labor shortages.
No academic background (university degree) is usually required.
Ability to change jobs within the same specified industry.
Receive the same salary as Japanese workers in the same role.
Eligible for various forms of support from the host company, including Japanese language training.
required_documents: Valid passport
One visa application form (two for nationals of Russia, CIS countries, or Georgia)
One recent photograph (two for nationals of Russia, CIS countries, or Georgia)
Certificate of Eligibility (COE) - original or one copy, or a printed copy if electronic
Skills evaluation test pass certificate
Japanese language test pass certificate (JLPT N4 or JFT-Basic), unless exempt (e.g., for those who completed Technical Intern Training (ii))
Employment contract specifying wages equal to a Japanese worker in the same role
Support plan from the accepting organization or a registered support organization
Tax and social-insurance documents for the employer
Health certificate
Copy of the Chinese Family Register (for Chinese nationals)
Temporary Residence Permit or Residence Certificate (for Chinese nationals, if applicable)
application_process_steps: Pass the sector-specific skills test and a Japanese language test (unless exempt).
Sign an employment contract with a Japanese accepting organization.
The prospective employer in Japan applies for a Certificate of Eligibility (COE) with the regional Immigration Services Agency office (this typically takes 1 to 3 months).
Once the COE is issued, it is sent to the applicant.
The applicant submits the COE, passport, and visa application to the Japanese embassy or consulate in their country of residence (visa stamping usually takes about one week).
Upon visa issuance, the applicant enters Japan, receives a Residence Card at the port of entry, and registers their address at the local municipal office within 14 days.

visas.name: Specified Skilled Worker Type 2
visas.description: The Specified Skilled Worker Type 2 (SSW2) visa is designed for foreign nationals who possess advanced and proficient skills in specific industry fields, enabling them to work long-term in Japan. Unlike SSW Type 1, this visa allows for indefinite renewals and the accompaniment of family members, serving as a direct pathway to permanent residency.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is a skilled foreign worker who has demonstrated advanced, field-specific skills, often after gaining experience under SSW Type 1, and wishes to establish long-term residence and work in Japan with their family.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Years spent under the SSW Type 2 status count towards Japan's general permanent residency requirement of 10 years of continuous residence, including at least 5 years in a work-eligible status. Successful applicants must also demonstrate good conduct, consistent tax and social insurance compliance, and no criminal record.
visas.renewal_conditions: Applicants must continue to meet the Type 2 skill level and be employed in a designated qualifying field, demonstrate consistent compliance with Japanese tax obligations and social insurance payments, and have no immigration law violations.
benefits: No upper limit on the length of stay, with the visa being indefinitely renewable.
Allows family members (spouse and children) to join the worker in Japan as dependents.
Years spent on SSW Type 2 count towards the general permanent residency requirements.
Permits working in one of the designated industries in Japan.
Salary must be equal to or higher than that of Japanese workers in the same role.
required_documents: Completed application form (to be filled by applicant and company).
Valid passport and a recent photograph (4 cm x 3 cm).
SSW Type 2 skills exam certificate for the relevant field.
Employment contract with the qualifying employer in Japan.
Employer's supporting documents (e.g., company registration, financial statements).
Current Residence Card (if already in Japan).
Medical examination report/Health certificate.

Documents related to pension, health insurance premiums, and taxes (e.g., Taxation Certificate, Certificate of Tax Payment, Withholding Tax Slip, copy of National Health Insurance Card, National Health Insurance Payment Certificate).
Certificate of Eligibility (COE) application form (if applying from overseas, completed by prospective employer).
Proof of financial ability to support dependents (if applying for family visas).
application_process_steps: Verify that your industry field is one of the designated fields for SSW Type 2.
Pass the field-specific SSW Type 2 skills measurement test, which assesses advanced technical knowledge and practical skills.
Secure an employment contract with a qualified Japanese employer willing to sponsor your SSW Type 2 visa.
Gather all necessary documents, including personal identification, employment records, and examination certificates.
Apply for the Certificate of Eligibility (if applying from overseas) or for a change/renewal of status of residence at a regional Immigration Services Agency office in Japan.
Upon approval, receive your new or updated Residence Card, which will reflect your SSW Type 2 status.

visas.name: Student
visas.description: The Student visa (Status of Residence 'Student') is for foreign nationals who wish to pursue full-time studies at an accredited educational institution in Japan, such as a university, junior college, college of technology, specialized training college, or Japanese language school. It allows the holder to reside in Japan for the purpose of their studies.
visas.target_applicant: Individuals who have received an offer of admission from a recognized educational institution in Japan and can demonstrate sufficient financial means to cover their tuition and living expenses.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Long-term residency on a student visa can contribute to eligibility for permanent residency in Japan after fulfilling specific residency duration and other criteria under the Immigration Control Act.
visas.renewal_conditions: Must maintain enrollment in an educational institution, adhere to visa conditions (e.g., work hour limits), and meet attendance requirements.
visas.tax_implications: Students are required to enroll in Japan's National Health Insurance (NHI) at a reduced student rate. Standard resident tax rules apply otherwise.
benefits: Opportunity to pursue higher education or language studies in Japan.
Permission to work part-time up to 28 hours per week during term time, and up to 40 hours per week during long breaks, with a separate work permit.
Access to Japan's National Health Insurance system.
Potential path to long-term residency in Japan.
required_documents: Valid passport
One visa application form (two for nationals of Russia, CIS countries or Georgia)
One photograph (two for nationals of Russia, CIS countries or Georgia)
Certificate of Eligibility (COE) - original or copy (electronic COE is accepted)
Letter of Admission or Certificate of Enrollment from the Japanese educational institution
Proof of financial support (e.g., bank statements showing sufficient funds, scholarship award letters, or a financial guarantee from a sponsor)
Financial sponsor's income certificate covering the past year (if applicable)
Documentation identifying the source of funds (if applicable)
Academic transcripts and graduation certificate from most recent schools
Statement of reason for study (sometimes required)
Proof of relationship with financial sponsor (if applicable, e.g., birth certificate)
application_process_steps: Obtain admission from a recognized Japanese educational institution.
The educational institution (or a proxy) applies for a Certificate of Eligibility (COE) on your behalf with the Immigration Services Agency of Japan.
Once the COE is issued and sent to you, gather all required documents for the visa application.
Submit your visa application, COE, passport, photographs, and other required documents to a Japanese embassy or consulate in your home country/region.
Receive your Student Visa.

Upon arrival in Japan, immigration will issue your Residence Card and you can apply for a 'Permission to Engage in Activity Other Than That Permitted Under the Status of Residence Previously Granted' (work permit) at the airport or later at an immigration office.

visas.name: Business Manager (Investor/Business Manager)
visas.description: The Business Manager visa (officially 'Business Manager' Status of Residence) is a legal pathway for foreign nationals to live in Japan and establish, manage, or invest in a business. It grants full authority to lead and administer a company within Japan, allowing day-to-day management or executive decision-making.
visas.target_applicant: This visa is tailored for aspiring entrepreneurs with capital, strategic investors actively managing a Japanese business, or foreign nationals appointed to key managerial or executive positions in Japanese companies.
visas.path_to_residency_description: General eligibility for Permanent Residency requires 10 years of continuous legal residence in Japan. This can be fast-tracked through the Highly Skilled Foreign Professional (HSP) route, allowing application after 3 years for those scoring 70+ points, or after 1 year for those scoring 80+ points on the immigration scorecard.
visas.renewal_conditions: The business must remain active, financially sound, and continue to meet all current requirements, including the JPY 30,000,000 capital, employing at least one full-time employee, and maintaining Japanese language proficiency (as per October 2025 revisions). Applicants must also comply with tax, labor, and social insurance obligations.
benefits: Long-term stability with initial stays typically ranging from 1 to 5 years, and renewability based on business performance.
Provides a clear pathway to permanent residency in Japan, potentially fast-tracked for highly skilled professionals.
Allows the holder to sponsor their spouse and dependent children to live in Japan under a Dependent Visa.
Grants full legal rights to run, manage, and administer their company within Japan.
Japan has double taxation agreements with many countries, which can help avoid being taxed twice on the same income.
required_documents: Application form, passport-size photo, original and photocopy of passport (or residence card if already in Japan).
Curriculum Vitae (CV) and career history showing at least 3 years of management experience or a relevant master's/doctoral/professional degree.
Documents certifying academic background (diploma) if applicable.
Certified copy of Business License or Incorporation documents (e.g., Certificate of Incorporation, Articles of Incorporation).
Evidence of office space (lease agreement and photos of the dedicated business office).
Financial statements (if applicable).
Proof of JPY 30,000,000 capital investment and its source.
Detailed business plan, expert-verified by a Small and Medium Enterprise Management Consultant, CPA, or licensed tax accountant.
Employment contracts and social insurance records for at least one full-time employee residing in Japan.
Documents clarifying Japanese language proficiency (e.g., JLPT N2 or higher certificate, or explanation if another employee meets this).
application_process_steps: Undergo an eligibility check and consultation, confirming all requirements are met.
Establish the company in Japan (e.g., Kabushiki Kaisha or Godo Kaisha) with at least JPY 30,000,000 capital and secure a dedicated, independent office space.
Hire at least one full-time employee who resides in Japan and establish a Japanese language operation framework.
Draft a detailed business plan and obtain its verification from a qualified professional (e.g., SME Management Consultant).
Prepare all required supporting documents, including evidence of capital, employee records, and personal credentials.
File the Certificate of Eligibility (CoE) application with the Immigration Services Agency, respond to any queries, and upon issuance, apply for the visa at a Japanese embassy/consulate.

visas.name: Journalist
visas.description: The Journalist visa in Japan is for foreign nationals engaged in news coverage and other journalistic activities. It allows individuals, including reporters, editors, cameramen, and announcers, to work in Japan for foreign media organizations, either as employees or freelancers with contracts.
visas.target_applicant: Journalists, photographers, editors, news cameramen, and announcers who are dispatched by or have a contract with a foreign media organization to conduct journalistic activities in Japan.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The Journalist visa is a long-term visa that can lead to permanent residency after a sufficiently long period of continuous stay in Japan, similar to other work visas. Specific timeframes are not detailed but generally require long-term residence.
visas.renewal_conditions: Must continue to engage in activities that fall under the 'Journalist' status of residence and demonstrate sufficient remuneration to sustain stay in Japan.
benefits: Ability to reside and work legally in Japan as a journalist.
Potential for long-term stays with periods of 1, 3, or 5 years.
Renewable visa, allowing continuous residence for ongoing journalistic work.
Covers a broad range of journalistic activities including reporting, filming, editing, and broadcasting.
Freelance journalists with contracts from foreign media organizations may be eligible.
required_documents: Letter from employer outlining assignment in Japan (if employed by a foreign media organization)
Press ID or credentials
Past articles or evidence of journalistic work
Proof of a continuous contract with an overseas news organization (including for freelancers)
Documents clarifying activities and an outline of the foreign journalistic organization (for Category 2 applicants, those not employed by an organization that issues an FPR Card)
Certificate of employment (for representatives of freelance journalists applying as a media organization)
Visa application form
Passport
Photo
application_process_steps: Gather required documents, including proof of employment or contract with a foreign media organization and evidence of journalistic work.
Submit the visa application to the Embassy or Consulate-General of Japan with jurisdiction over your place of residence.
If applicable, obtain a Certificate of Eligibility (COE) from the Immigration Services Agency of Japan, which is generally recommended for long-term stays.
Attend an in-person interview if required (some embassies may require this).
Receive notification of visa decision and collect the visa from the diplomatic mission.
Upon arrival in Japan, register with relevant authorities and, if applicable, apply for a Foreign Press Registration Card through the Foreign Press Center Japan (FPCJ).

visas.name: Legal/Accounting Services
visas.description: The 'Legal/Accounting Services' status of residence in Japan allows foreign nationals to engage in exclusive business activities related to law or accounting, provided they hold specific Japanese legal or accounting qualifications, or recognized foreign equivalents. This visa category is for professionals whose work requires licenses or registrations under Japanese law.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are foreign lawyers, foreign certified public accountants, or individuals holding specific Japanese legal qualifications (e.g., judicial scriveners, tax accountants, patent attorneys) who are registered with the relevant Japanese authorities to perform exclusive professional activities.
visas.path_to_residency_description: This visa can lead to permanent residency. General requirements for permanent residency include residing in Japan continuously for at least 10 years (with at least 5 years on a work visa), demonstrating good conduct, possessing sufficient assets or ability to make an independent living, and holding a current visa with a period of stay of 3 years or more. Shorter periods may apply for Highly Skilled Professionals.
visas.renewal_conditions: Applicants must maintain their professional qualifications and registrations, continue to engage in the permitted activities, maintain good conduct, and fulfill all obligations including tax payments. The period of stay granted upon renewal depends on the applicant's circumstances.
visas.tax_implications: Holders of this status of residence are generally subject to standard Japanese tax laws as residents, including income tax, consumption tax, and local inhabitant taxes. No special tax exemptions or treatments for this visa category were identified.
benefits: Permission to engage in exclusive legal or accounting professional activities in Japan.
Ability to reside in Japan for extended periods (up to 5 years).
Option for spouse and children to obtain dependent visas.
Potential path to permanent residency in Japan.
required_documents: Application for Certificate of Eligibility (COE)
Photograph (meeting specified requirements)
Return envelope (standard size with address and stamp for registered mail)
Documentation certifying possession of a relevant Japanese qualification (copy of license, certificate, etc.)
Japanese translation for any documents in foreign languages
Passport (for visa application after COE)
application_process_steps: Gather all necessary documents, including proof of Japanese legal/accounting qualifications and personal identification.
Have your sponsor (e.g., employer) in Japan apply for a Certificate of Eligibility (COE) at a regional Immigration Services Bureau.
Once the COE is issued and sent to you by your sponsor, prepare your visa application form.
Apply for the visa stamp at the Japanese embassy or consulate in your home country, presenting your COE, passport, and other required documents.
After visa issuance, travel to Japan and receive your Residence Card at the port of entry.
Within 14 days of resident registration, enroll in the National Health Insurance system at your local municipal office if not covered by employer-provided health insurance.

visas.name: Researcher
visas.description: The Researcher visa (Status of Residence: 'Researcher') in Japan is for foreign nationals engaged in research work under a contract with a public or private institution in Japan. This excludes educational and research activities primarily conducted at universities, which fall under the 'Professor' status. It allows individuals to conduct research for specified periods.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are researchers, investigators, and similar professionals contracted by research institutes, government agencies, independent administrative agencies, public interest corporations, or private companies in Japan.
visas.path_to_residency_description: While the Researcher visa itself allows long-term stay, highly skilled professionals (which can include researchers) may be eligible for the 'Highly Skilled Professional' visa, which offers faster access to a Permanent Resident visa in Japan.
visas.renewal_conditions: Must maintain income threshold comparable to Japanese nationals and continue research activities under contract.
benefits: Allows engaging in research activities under contract in Japan.
Periods of stay can be up to 5 years.
Dependents (family members) are allowed to accompany the researcher.
Provides a pathway to potential long-term residency in Japan.
Host institutions often assist with the Certificate of Eligibility application process.
required_documents: Application for Certificate of Eligibility (COE)
Resume clearly indicating relevant organizations, activities, and employment periods
Documents proving research experience period or graduation certificate from a university or equivalent (or proof of equivalent/higher education/advanced specialist qualification)
Documents certifying the accepting institution's category (for COE application)
Passport
Visa application form
Photograph (4cm×3cm, no background, no hats, name on reverse)
Letter of acceptance (from the host institution)
Certificate of payment (if applicable)
Documents clarifying the capital relationship and existence of a business office in Japan (for secondments to foreign corporations)
Japanese translation for documents prepared in a foreign language
Certificates issued in Japan must be dated within 3 months of the application date
application_process_steps: The host institution in Japan applies for a Certificate of Eligibility (COE) on behalf of the researcher with the Immigration Services Agency of Japan.
Upon issuance, the COE is sent from the Immigration Services Agency to the host institution, and then forwarded to the foreign researcher overseas.
The foreign researcher submits their visa application, along with the COE and other required documents, to the Japanese embassy or consulate in their country of residence.
The Japanese embassy or consulate examines the application and issues the visa.
Upon arrival in Japan, researchers staying for more than 3 months must apply for a Resident Card at their local city/town office.

visas.name: Instructor
visas.description: The 'Instructor' visa in Japan is for foreign nationals engaged in language instruction or other educational activities at elementary schools, junior high schools, high schools, secondary schools, special support schools, vocational schools, and other equivalent educational institutions. It facilitates the employment of foreign teachers in the Japanese education sector.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is an individual with a university degree or equivalent, or a relevant teaching license, who has secured a teaching position at an eligible public or private educational institution in Japan.
visas.path_to_residency_description: While not immediate, individuals holding work visas like the Instructor visa can typically apply for permanent residency after a period of continuous residence in Japan, often requiring at least 10 years of residency with a portion of that time spent on a work visa.
visas.renewal_conditions: To renew, applicants must provide proof of continued employment, updated contract terms, and demonstrate a clean immigration record.
benefits: Allows legal employment as an instructor in public elementary, junior high, and high schools, and certain other educational institutions in Japan.
Initial validity periods of 1, 3, or 5 years are available.
The visa is renewable, allowing for continued residence and work in Japan.
Allows dependants (spouse and children) to apply for a family stay visa to join the main visa holder.
Provides a potential path to permanent residency in Japan after meeting specific long-term residency requirements.
required_documents: Valid passport (at least 6 months remaining).
Certificate of Eligibility (COE) (original or email copy).
Completed visa application form.
Passport-sized photograph.
University degree certificate (certified copy) or teaching license.
Official transcripts (if applicable).
Proof of income/tax records (for renewal applications).
New employment contract or employer letter (for renewal applications).
Residence Card (for renewal applications).
Any additional documents requested by the Japanese Embassy or Consulate.
application_process_steps: Secure a formal job offer from an eligible Japanese educational institution that is willing to sponsor your visa.
Your prospective employer in Japan will apply for a Certificate of Eligibility (COE) on your behalf at a regional immigration office.
Gather and provide all necessary personal and educational documents to your employer for the COE application.
Upon approval, receive the Certificate of Eligibility (COE) from your employer.
Submit your visa application, along with your COE, valid passport, completed application form, and passport-sized photo, to the nearest Japanese Embassy or Consulate in your country of residence.
Upon arrival in Japan, receive your Residence Card at the airport and register your address at the local city hall within 14 days, and enroll in the National Health Insurance system.

visas.name: Engineer/Specialist in Humanities/International Services
visas.description: This is a comprehensive work visa status for foreign professionals in Japan, encompassing three categories: Engineer (natural sciences, IT, mechanical/electrical engineering), Specialist in Humanities (law, economics, business administration, marketing, HR, finance), and International Services (translation, interpretation, language teaching, design, overseas sales). It allows individuals to work for public or private institutions in Japan in roles requiring specialized knowledge, academic expertise, or international business skills.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is a foreign national with a relevant university degree or significant professional experience, who has secured a job offer from a Japanese employer for a professional role aligning with their qualifications.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The standard path to permanent residency requires 10 years of continuous residence in Japan, including at least 5 years on a work visa. Time spent on this visa counts towards eligibility for permanent residency.
visas.renewal_conditions: Renewal requires re-examination of the applicant's current job duties, employment conditions (including remuneration equal to or higher than Japanese nationals), and past residence history (e.g., tax payments, compliance with notification obligations). If the applicant changed jobs, the new role must continue to meet the visa requirements.
benefits: Allows long-term work in Japan in professional fields.
Provides a pathway to permanent residency in Japan.
Permits dependants (spouse and children) to join on dependent visas.
Offers flexibility to switch employers within the same visa category, provided immigration is notified.
required_documents: Valid passport
Recent passport-sized photo (4 cm x 3 cm)
Certificate of Eligibility (COE) - original, copy, or digital PDF
Visa application form
Diploma or graduation certificate (with apostille or notarization if requested)
Academic transcript
CV/resume listing dates, employers, and duties
Professional certifications (especially for IT applicants using certification route)
Evidence of work experience (employment letters specifying dates and duties) if qualifying based on practical experience
Employment contract from a Japanese company
Company documents (e.g., corporate registration, tax/social insurance records) - typically submitted by employer
Detailed explanation of why the role qualifies for the visa category - typically submitted by employer

Japanese language proficiency evidence (JLPT N2 or higher, BJT score 400+, or other specific criteria) if working for Category 3 or 4 companies in customer-facing roles using Japanese (effective April 15, 2026)
For Chinese nationals: Copy of Chinese Family Register, Temporary Residence Permit or Residence Certificate (if applicable)
application_process_steps: Secure a qualifying job offer from a Japanese employer and sign an employment contract.
The employer (or an immigration lawyer on their behalf) files the Certificate of Eligibility (COE) application with the regional Immigration Services Agency (ISA) office in Japan.
Wait for COE issuance, which typically takes 2 to 3 months. A digital COE can be received by email.
The employer sends the issued COE (physical or digital) to the applicant overseas.
The applicant applies for the visa at the Japanese embassy or consulate in their country of residence, submitting the COE, passport, visa application form, and photo.
The embassy/consulate processes the visa application, usually taking 1 to 2 weeks.
Enter Japan within 90 days of COE issuance and register your address at the local municipal office within 14 days of determining residence.

visas.name: Intra-company Transferee
visas.description: The Intra-company Transferee visa is a special work visa in Japan allowing employees of multinational companies to transfer temporarily to a Japanese branch, subsidiary, or affiliate. It facilitates the relocation of skilled staff, managers, executives, or employees with specific expertise for business operations, management, engineering, or international services within the same corporate group.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are employees who have been continuously employed at an overseas office of a multinational company for at least one year immediately prior to the transfer and will perform specialized duties in Japan similar to those under the Engineer/Specialist in Humanities/International Services category.
visas.path_to_residency_description: While not explicitly detailed as a direct path to permanent residency in the provided sources, the visa allows for long-term stays (up to 5 years per period) and is a category under which 'long-term residency pathways' are mentioned as potentially evolving.
visas.renewal_conditions: Must maintain eligibility requirements, including continuous employment within the corporate group and performing duties equivalent to Engineer/Specialist in Humanities/International Services, with compensation at or above that of a Japanese national for the same work.
visas.tax_implications: Tax, payroll, and social security implications depend on whether the transfer is an assignment (employee remains on home country payroll with taxes due in Japan on Japanese-sourced income) or a permanent basis (employee moved to Japanese payroll). Tax position can change further depending on assignment duration (e.g., under or over 6 months).
benefits: Allows relocation to a Japan office within the same multinational corporate group.
Does not require a university degree, focusing instead on one year of prior continuous employment and specialized expertise.
Facilitates sharing of skills and expertise within a company, ensuring uniform standards and operational continuity.
Provides international exposure and career opportunities for employees.
Flexibility of duties within the Engineer/Specialist in Humanities/International Services categories.
required_documents: Passport
Visa application form (two forms for nationals of Russia, CIS countries, or Georgia)
Photograph (two photographs for nationals of Russia, CIS countries, or Georgia)
Certificate of Eligibility (COE) - original or one copy (electronic COE copy also accepted)
Resume or Curriculum Vitae
Educational certificates (if applicable)
Proof of employment (employment certificate from the overseas entity covering at least the last 12 months)
Copy of the transfer order or assignment letter
Company documentation (overview, registration certificate, financial statements of the Japanese branch)

Documents proving the existence of the overseas office where the applicant was employed (e.g., corporate registration documents, proof of business operations like tax records, transaction history) (mandatory from April 1, 2026)
Documents proving the existence of the office in Japan where the applicant will be active (e.g., real estate registration, photographs of office, floor plans) (mandatory from April 1, 2026)
Proof of social insurance enrollment abroad (new since April 2026)
Proof of foreign tax payment status (new since April 2026)
For nationals of the Philippines, Nepal, or Vietnam: documentation under the Japan Pre-Entry Tuberculosis Screening (JPETS) program (in effect since 2025)
Copy of Chinese Family Register (for Chinese nationals)
Temporary Residence Permit or Residence Certificate (for Chinese nationals without a family register in the jurisdiction)
application_process_steps: The Japanese receiving company applies for a Certificate of Eligibility (COE) with the Immigration Services Agency of Japan on behalf of the employee (typically 1-3 months processing time).
Once the COE is issued, the applicant applies for the Intra-company Transferee visa at a Japanese embassy or consulate in their country of residence.
Submit the COE (original or copy), passport, visa application form, and supporting documents to the embassy/consulate.
The visa application typically takes 5-10 working days to process.
Upon arrival in Japan, the employee receives a residence card at the airport.

visas.name: Skilled Labor
visas.description: The 'Skilled Labor' program in Japan is primarily covered by the Specified Skilled Worker (SSW) visa, aimed at foreign nationals with job-ready skills to address labor shortages in specific industries, and the Highly Skilled Professional (HSP) visa, for individuals in higher-skill, higher-income professional roles.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant for SSW is someone with practical skills and Japanese language ability (JLPT N4 or higher) in fields like nursing care, construction, or manufacturing, while for HSP, it's a professional with advanced academic or technical expertise and a high income, scoring at least 70 points in a points-based system.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Specified Skilled Worker Type 2 is often considered a pathway to long-term residence in Japan. The Highly Skilled Professional visa offers a fast-track to permanent residency for those maintaining at least 70 points and fulfilling other requirements like stable employment and consistent tax and pension payments.
visas.renewal_conditions: For Specified Skilled Worker Type 1, the total stay is capped at 5 years. Specified Skilled Worker Type 2 has no upper limit on length of stay and is renewable. Highly Skilled Professional visa holders must maintain their points threshold and consistent residency with up-to-date tax and pension payments.
benefits: Addresses labor shortages in key industries for SSW visa holders.
Allows family members to join for Specified Skilled Worker Type 2 and Highly Skilled Professional visa holders.
No upper limit on length of stay for Specified Skilled Worker Type 2 and Highly Skilled Professional visa holders, making it a pathway to long-term residency.
Fast-track to permanent residency for Highly Skilled Professional visa holders.
Opportunity to work in Japan without a university degree for many Specified Skilled Worker Type 1 roles.
required_documents: Passport
Visa application form (one or two depending on nationality)
Photograph(s) (one or two depending on nationality)
Certificate of Eligibility (COE) (original or copy)
Sector-specific skills evaluation test pass certificate (for SSW)
Japanese language test pass certificate (JLPT N4/JFT-Basic for SSW Type 1, or higher for specific roles like nursing care, taxi/bus, railway train operation)
Employment contract specifying wages equal to a Japanese worker in the same role
Support plan from the accepting organization or a registered support organization (for SSW)
Tax and social-insurance documents for the employer
Health certificate
Pre-Entry Tuberculosis Screening certificate (for nationals of Philippines, Vietnam, Indonesia, Nepal, Myanmar, and China for medium to long-term visas)
Documents proving points (such as diplomas, salary documents, and employment contracts for HSP)
Documents from employer (contract and company information for HSP)
Copy of Chinese Family Register (for Chinese nationals)
Temporary Residence Permit or Residence Certificate (for Chinese nationals if not registered in jurisdiction)
Curriculum vitae (for Skilled Labor visa, Chinese nationals)
application_process_steps: Pass the sector-specific skills test and Japanese language test (for SSW).
Sign an employment contract with a Japanese accepting organization.
The employer in Japan files the Certificate of Eligibility (COE) application with the regional Immigration Services Agency office.
Once the COE is issued, it is sent to the applicant.
The applicant submits the COE, passport, and visa application to the Japanese embassy or consulate in their country of residence.
Receive the visa and present it at immigration inspection upon arrival in Japan.

visas.name: Dependent (Spouse or Child of a Foreign National with a long-term visa)
visas.description: The Dependent Visa in Japan is a status of residence that allows the spouse and children of a foreign national holding a long-term visa (such as a work or student visa) to live with them in Japan. This visa is granted on the condition that the dependent family members are financially supported by the primary visa holder.
visas.target_applicant: Spouses and dependent children (typically unmarried and under 18, though adult children may be considered under special circumstances) of foreign nationals legally residing in Japan under valid long-term residence statuses like Engineer/Specialist in Humanities/International Services, Business Manager, Student, or Highly Skilled Professional. Parents, siblings, and other relatives are not eligible.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Dependent visa holders can apply for permanent residency, often in conjunction with the primary visa holder. Spouses of Japanese nationals or Permanent Residents may be eligible to apply for permanent residency after maintaining a substantive marital life for 3 years and residing continuously in Japan for at least 1 year. For other dependents, the path typically aligns with the primary visa holder's eligibility, generally requiring 10 years of continuous residence in Japan, including 5 years on a work-permitting status.
visas.renewal_conditions: The primary visa holder's residency and job status must remain stable, with sufficient income to support the family. Children of compulsory school age must be attending school. Dependent visa holders with a work permit must not exceed 28 hours of part-time work per week. Compliance with all immigration requirements, tax payments, and social insurance contributions is essential.
benefits: Allows family members (spouse and children) to reside together in Japan.
Children can attend school in Japan.
Opportunity to apply for permission to engage in part-time work up to 28 hours per week.
Provides a pathway to permanent residency under certain conditions.
required_documents: Application form for Certificate of Eligibility (COE)
Passport copy of the accompanying family member(s)
One photograph (4cm x 3cm, taken within the last 3 months, full-face view, no hat, plain background)
Original marriage certificate (for spouse) or birth certificate (for child) (with English or Japanese translation if in another language)
Proof of income of the primary visa holder (e.g., tax certificates, employment certificate, employment contract, bank statements)
Sponsor's passport or residence card copy
Residence certificate (Jumin-hyo) of the primary visa holder in Japan
Letter of Guarantee (if applying without a COE or as requested by the embassy/consulate)
Written explanation detailing support for adult children or those joining later (if applicable)
application_process_steps: Confirm that the family members (spouse, children) meet the eligibility criteria for a dependent visa.
Gather all required documents, including proof of relationship, sponsor's financial stability, passports, and photographs.
The primary visa holder (sponsor) in Japan applies for a Certificate of Eligibility (COE) at a regional immigration office. This can also be done online.
Once the COE is issued (typically within 1-3 months), the sponsor sends the original document to the family member residing abroad.

The family member submits the COE along with other necessary documents to the Japanese embassy or consulate in their home country to obtain the visa (visa issuance generally takes 5 working days to 2 weeks).
Travel to Japan; a Residence Card will be issued upon entry.
If part-time work is desired, apply for 'Permission to Engage in Activity Other Than That Permitted Under the Status of Residence' at the Immigration Bureau.

visas.name: Spouse or Child of Japanese National
visas.description: This visa status is for foreign nationals who are legally married to a Japanese national or are the biological or specially adopted child of a Japanese national, allowing them to reside in Japan. It facilitates family unity and provides a pathway for spouses and children to live long-term with their Japanese family members in Japan.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is a foreign national who has a legally recognized marriage to a Japanese citizen or is a child (biological or specially adopted) of a Japanese citizen, seeking to live together in Japan.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Holders of the 'Spouse or Child of Japanese National' visa can apply for permanent residency. For spouses, they generally must have been married for at least three years and resided in Japan for over one year. For biological or specially adopted children, they must have resided in Japan for at least one year. There are also general requirements like continuous residence in Japan for 10 years (though exceptions apply for spouses/children), good conduct, and financial stability.
visas.renewal_conditions: Must maintain a genuine marital relationship, continue to reside in Japan with the Japanese national, and meet financial support requirements. The Immigration Services Agency reviews family structure and household income to determine renewal period.
visas.tax_implications: Standard resident tax rules apply. There are no special tax exemptions or statuses associated with this visa category.
benefits: Allows legal residence in Japan with a Japanese spouse or parent.
No restrictions on working hours or type of work, unlike many other visa categories.
Provides a clearer path to permanent residency compared to other visa types.
Periods of stay can be up to 5 years, offering stability.
Facilitates a smoother immigration process if a Certificate of Eligibility (COE) is obtained.
required_documents: Valid passport
Visa application form
Photograph (specified size, e.g., 45mm x 45mm or 2x2 inches, depending on embassy/consulate)
Certificate of Eligibility (COE) - original or copy (highly recommended, though application without is possible but takes longer). If electronic COE, present at counter or submit printed copy.
Official copy of the Japanese spouse's or parent's family register (Koseki Tohon or Koseki Shohon), issued within three months, showing registered marriage/birth.
Marriage certificate (for spouse) or birth certificate (for child) issued by the applicant's country of nationality.
Two letters of guarantee from the Japanese spouse/relative (content and specific requirements may vary by embassy/consulate).
Documents proving financial support (e.g., resident tax certificate, tax payment certificate, certificate of employment, certificate of tax payment for the guarantor/Japanese spouse).
Certificate of residence (Jumin-hyo) listing all household members.
Questionnaire (may be required).
Evidence of a genuine relationship (e.g., wedding photos, communication records) for spouses.
application_process_steps: Gather all required documents from both Japan and the applicant's home country, including necessary translations.

The Japanese spouse or a representative in Japan applies for a Certificate of Eligibility (COE) at a regional immigration authority under the Immigration Services Agency of Japan. This step is highly recommended.
Once the COE is issued (average processing time is 3-4 months), it is sent to the applicant abroad.
The applicant then applies for the visa at a Japanese embassy or consulate in their country of residence, submitting the COE and other required documents.
After the visa is issued (typically 5 business days with a COE), the applicant enters Japan within 3 months of the COE's issuance date.
Upon arrival, the applicant completes necessary registrations like address registration at the City Hall and enrollment in National Health Insurance.

visas.name: Spouse or Child of Permanent Resident
visas.description: This visa (Status of Residence) is for the foreign spouse or biological minor, unmarried child of a person holding Permanent Resident status in Japan. It allows them to reside in Japan with their permanent resident family member and can serve as a pathway to obtaining their own permanent residency.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is a foreign national who is legally married to a Japanese Permanent Resident, or a minor, unmarried biological child of a Japanese Permanent Resident.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Spouses of Permanent Residents can apply for permanent residency after maintaining a genuine marital relationship for three years or more and continuously residing in Japan for at least one year. Children (biological, minor, unmarried) of Permanent Residents can apply for permanent residency after continuously residing in Japan for at least one year. Applicants must also meet general permanent residency requirements, including good conduct and fulfilling public obligations.
visas.renewal_conditions: Maintaining a genuine marital relationship (for spouses), continuing to be financially supported (for children), and fulfilling public obligations such as timely payment of taxes, public pension contributions, and public health insurance premiums.
benefits: Ability to live legally in Japan with a permanent resident spouse or parent
Opportunity to apply for Permanent Residency after meeting specific criteria (e.g., 1 year residency for children, 1 year residency and 3 years marriage for spouses)
No restrictions on period of stay once permanent residency is obtained
Work permitted with prior permission from immigration authorities
required_documents: Passport
Visa application form (one or two depending on nationality)
Photograph (one or two depending on nationality)
Certificate of Eligibility (COE) - original or copy (recommended for smooth processing)
Copy of the Permanent Resident spouse's Japanese Residence Card (在留カード)
Copy of the Resident Record (住民票) showing both spouses (if already living together in Japan)
Marriage certificate(s) from both countries with Japanese translation (for spouses)
Letter of explanation detailing the history of the relationship (in Japanese, for spouses)
Photographs together as a couple, messages, call records, or other evidence of relationship authenticity (for spouses)
Birth certificate or other official documents to prove blood relationship (for children)
Certificate of employment of the permanent resident spouse/parent
Income-related documents (e.g., resident tax payment certificate, tax payment certificate, certificate of withholding tax) of the permanent resident spouse/parent for the most recent year(s)
Guarantor letter and documentation from the permanent resident spouse/parent
application_process_steps: Obtain a Certificate of Eligibility (COE) from the Immigration Services Agency of Japan (highly recommended, typically applied for by the permanent resident in Japan).
Gather all required documents, including passport, application form, photograph, and relationship/financial proofs.
Complete the visa application form.
Submit the application and documents to a Japanese embassy or consulate in the applicant's country of residence.
Undergo screening by immigration authorities.
Receive visa issuance.

visas.name: Long-Term Resident
visas.description: The 'Long-Term Resident' (Teijusha) status is granted to foreign nationals with special personal, family, or humanitarian ties to Japan, who do not fall under any other specific residence status but are recognized by the Minister of Justice as having special circumstances that justify a long-term stay. This visa allows for a relatively free lifestyle, including unrestricted employment, and serves as a pathway to permanent residency.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants include descendants of Japanese nationals (e.g., Nikkei), spouses or children of Japanese nationals or permanent residents under specific conditions (like after divorce or death of a spouse), children raised in Japan under special humanitarian considerations, or individuals approved for other humanitarian or social reasons by the Minister of Justice.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Time spent in Japan under a Long-Term Resident Visa generally counts toward eligibility for Permanent Residency (PR). Many holders become eligible for PR after living in Japan for approximately 5 years, provided they demonstrate stable income or financial support, good conduct, and tax compliance.
visas.renewal_conditions: Must continue to meet the conditions under which the visa was granted, maintain stable residence in Japan, comply with Japanese laws, and pay taxes properly.
benefits: Unrestricted employment in any industry or occupation, full-time, part-time, or self-employed, without requiring additional work permission.
Long-term stability with initial validity periods of up to 5 years and renewability.
Clear pathway to Permanent Residency in Japan, generally after 5 years of continuous residence.
Flexibility in daily life and activities as the status is not tied to a specific job or industry.
required_documents: Passport
Visa application form
Photograph
Certificate of Eligibility (original or copy) – recommended but not strictly mandatory, though applying without it can significantly prolong processing
Proof of family relationships (e.g., copy of family register for Chinese nationals, documents showing Japanese ancestry for Nikkei descendants)
Financial records (to demonstrate stable income or financial support, especially for PR pathway)
Written explanation of circumstances justifying the long-term stay
Supporting evidence showing strong ties to Japan
Criminal record certificate (for specific applicants like third-generation Japanese descendants)
application_process_steps: Identify if your individual circumstances align with the eligibility criteria for a Long-Term Resident visa.
Obtain a Certificate of Eligibility (COE) from the Immigration Services Agency of Japan, usually through a sponsor in Japan (this pre-screens the application and speeds up visa processing).
Submit the visa application form, passport, photograph, and COE (if obtained) along with other required supporting documents to the Japanese embassy or consulate in your country of residence.
For those already in Japan under another status, apply to change your status of residence to 'Long-Term Resident' at a regional immigration office due to changes in personal circumstances.
Await visa issuance after the application review.
Enter Japan with the issued visa and undergo immigration inspection to officially begin your stay as a 'Long-Term Resident'.

visas.name: Designated Activities (Future Creation Individual - J-Find)
visas.description: The 'Designated Activities (Future Creation Individual - J-Find)' visa is designed for recent graduates from top global universities who wish to come to Japan for job-hunting activities or to prepare for starting a business. It allows for a flexible stay of up to two years, during which holders can also engage in remunerative activities to support themselves.
visas.target_applicant: Individuals aged 18 or older who have graduated with a bachelor's, master's, or PhD degree from a university ranked in the top 100 of at least two major world rankings, and whose degree was awarded within the last five years before the application date.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The J-Find visa serves as a 'pre-employment preparation period.' Upon securing a job offer, holders can transition to a standard work visa (e.g., Engineer/Specialist in Humanities/International Services) or, if starting a business, to a Business Manager visa. These work/business visas can then lead to eligibility for permanent residency after meeting specific residency periods (e.g., typically 10 years, or shorter for Highly Skilled Professional visa holders).
visas.renewal_conditions: Applicants must demonstrate active engagement in job-hunting or business startup preparation activities during their stay to be eligible for renewal. The maximum total stay period is two years.
visas.tax_implications: Individuals staying in Japan for an extended period are generally considered tax residents from the start, meaning their worldwide income may be subject to Japanese taxation. For non-permanent residents (foreign nationals residing in Japan for 5 years or less within the last 10 years on a 'Table 1' visa, which includes J-Find), only Japan-sourced income and foreign-source income that is remitted into Japan are typically subject to Japanese income tax.
benefits: Permission to engage in job-hunting activities or business startup preparation in Japan.
Ability to work (part-time or full-time) to supplement living expenses, with relaxed restrictions on job type (excluding adult entertainment).
Spouses and children are permitted to accompany the visa holder on a dependent visa.
Initial period of stay typically 6 months or 1 year, renewable up to a maximum total of two years.
No requirement for an employer sponsor at the time of initial application.
required_documents: Passport
Visa Application Form (with a photograph)

Certificate of Eligibility (COE) - original or copy (if available, it simplifies the process and may negate the need for other documents like diploma proof, savings proof, activity description, and CV)
Documents proving the awarded qualification (diploma, academic transcripts) from an eligible university
Documents proving sufficient personal savings (e.g., bank balance certificate showing at least ¥200,000 JPY)
Description of intended activities (job-hunting plan or business startup preparation plan)
Curriculum Vitae (CV)
Pledge to undertake necessary procedures for joining Japan's National Health Insurance
application_process_steps: Confirm eligibility criteria, including university ranking, graduation date, age, and financial resources.
Gather all required documents, including passport, visa application form, photograph, diploma, proof of savings, activity plan, CV, and health insurance pledge.

Decide on the application route: either apply for a Certificate of Eligibility (COE) from within Japan (if currently residing there under another status) or apply directly for the visa at a Japanese embassy or consulate in your country of residence.
Submit the completed application and all supporting documents to the relevant Japanese diplomatic mission or immigration office.
Await the processing of the application and the issuance of the visa.
If applying from abroad, enter Japan with the issued visa; if applying from within Japan, your status of residence will be changed.

visas.name: Designated Activities (Long Stay for Sightseeing and Recreation)
visas.description: This visa, categorized as Designated Activities No. 40 (and No. 41 for an accompanying spouse), is for wealthy foreign nationals from visa-waiver countries who wish to stay in Japan for an extended period for tourism, recreation, and cultural enjoyment. It allows for a maximum stay of up to one year, initially granted for six months and renewable once.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are individuals aged 18 or older from visa-waiver countries with substantial personal savings, seeking to undertake long-term tourism and recreation in Japan.
visas.renewal_conditions: The visa is initially granted for six months and can be extended for an additional six months, allowing for a total stay of up to one year. An application for extension of period of stay must be made to the Regional Immigration Bureau before the initial six-month period expires, maintaining the eligibility requirements.
benefits: Extended stay in Japan for up to one year for tourism and recreation, without requiring frequent exits.
Opportunity for deep cultural immersion and exploration at a relaxed pace.
No requirement to work, invest, or start a business in Japan.
Allows an accompanying spouse to join under a similar Designated Activities No. 41 visa.
required_documents: Valid passport
Visa Application Form (with a passport-style photograph)
Certificate of Eligibility (CoE) (original or copy, or electronic CoE) issued by Immigration in Japan, or supporting documents if applying directly at a consulate
Schedule of Stay outlining planned activities in Japan
Documents proving savings of at least 30 million Japanese Yen, such as bank statements for the past 6 months showing current balance, deposits, and withdrawals
Documents proving private medical travel insurance which covers death, injury, and illness during the entire stay in Japan
For accompanying spouse: Marriage Certificate
If applying from outside of one's own country: Documents to prove legal residence or work in the country where the application is made
application_process_steps: Confirm nationality is from a visa-waiver country.
Gather all required documents, including passport, visa application form, photograph, schedule of stay, proof of at least ¥30 million JPY in savings, and proof of private medical travel insurance.
Obtain a Certificate of Eligibility (CoE) from the Immigration Services Agency in Japan (recommended, though direct application at an embassy/consulate may be possible).
Submit the complete visa application package to a Japanese embassy or consulate in your country of residence.
Attend any required interviews and provide additional information or documents if requested by the consular officer.

visas.name: Permanent Residency
visas.description: The Permanent Residency program in Japan grants foreign nationals the ability to reside in Japan indefinitely without restrictions on activities or period of stay, similar to a Japanese national (excluding voting rights). It is a highly sought-after status that provides long-term stability and numerous benefits.
